label: loc-iv-j420r
note: The project's own gold-standard reference case (RockSim's own CP for this exact file is independently hand-verified elsewhere) — 38.6mm mount. No saved simulation in the file itself. Previously used K400C, which turned out to be a REAL BUG: K400C is a 54mm-case motor (confirmed via ThrustCurve.org's own metadata), physically too wide for this file's 38.6mm motor mount -- caught by an explicit audit of every validation case's motor diameter against its rocket's real mount size. J420R is a real, currently-in-production 38mm AeroTech motor with a comparable average thrust to what "K400" implied (420N vs. 400N) -- picked as the closest real, correctly-sized substitute (confirmed present in BOTH OpenRocket's own bundled motor database and ThrustCurve.org's live API -- the first substitute tried, J340M, resolved live but wasn't in OpenRocket's bundled snapshot, so the Java harness couldn't use it). AeroTech doesn't make a 38mm K-class motor at all -- their 38mm case tops out around I/J class.

label: big-nuke-3e-m650w
note: 76mm mount. Real, vendor-saved simulation motor -- this exact file has 3 saved sims (M1297W/M650W/L850W), M650W picked as the mid-size one.

label: apogee-katana-k550w
note: 54mm mount. Real, vendor-saved simulation motor (this file has dozens, spanning I100-L990).

label: apogee-zephyr-g339n
note: 38.7mm mount. Real, vendor-saved simulation motor. (This file's saved sims also include H120-RL, but that exact designation no longer resolves on ThrustCurve.org -- confirmed directly, likely discontinued/renamed since the file was saved -- so G339N was used instead, still one of the file's own embedded choices.)

label: wildman-cerberus-h128w
note: 29mm mount. Freeform-fin geometry, not trapezoidal -- exercises a different code path than the LOC/Apogee cases above. (This file's saved sims list H160-SK/H180-SK/etc, but none of those exact designations resolve on ThrustCurve.org currently -- confirmed directly, likely a RockSim-internal or since-renamed motor database -- so H128W, a real, current, correctly-sized 29mm AeroTech H motor, was used instead.)

label: mach1-patriot-bt50-c6
note: 18mm mount, small/low-power end of the library. No saved simulation in the file, Estes C6 picked manually (classic, always-in-the-database motor -- same one OpenRocketCoreTest itself uses to sanity-check the motor DB, just C6 instead of B6). Manufacturer specified explicitly -- multiple vendors make a "C6", confirmed directly (ThrustCurve.org's own search also returns a Quest Aerospace C6) -- without pinning it, the Java harness and the TS motor-fixture fetch could each independently pick a DIFFERENT one sharing the same bare designation.
